content.Title: Other ACC/AHA Clinical Practice Guidelines Addressing Patients With Stage B HF

Details.Condition: Patients with an acute MI who have not developed HF symptoms treated in accordance with GDMT
Reference: 2013 ACCF/AHA Guideline for the Management of ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (51)
2014 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Management of Patients With Non–ST-Elevation Acute Coronary Syndromes (52)

Details.Condition: Coronary revascularization for patients without symptoms of HF in accordance with GDMT
Reference: 2015 ACC/AHA/SCAI Focused Update on Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Patients With ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (53)
2011 ACCF/AHA Guideline for Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Surgery (56)

Details.Condition: Valve replacement or repair for patients with hemodynamically significant valvular stenosis or regurgitation with no symptoms of HF in accordance with GDMT
Reference: 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease (57, 58)

Details.Condition: Patients with congenital heart disease that may increase the risk for the development of HF
Reference: 2018 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Management of Adults With Congenital Heart Disease (59)

Sections.Header: Nonpharmacological Interventions: Self-Care Support in HF

Recommendations.Description: Patients with HF should receive care from multidisciplinary teams to facilitate the implementation of GDMT, address potential barriers to self-care, reduce the risk of subsequent rehospitalization for HF, and improve survival (1-4).
Patients with HF should receive specific education and support to facilitate HF self-care in a multidisciplinary manner (2, 5-9).
In patients with HF, vaccinating against respiratory illnesses is reasonable to reduce mortality (10-16).

In adults with HF, screening for depression (17, 18), social isolation (19-22), frailty (23, 24), and low health literacy (25, 26) as risk factors for poor self-care is reasonable to improve management.

Comments: Avoid thiazolidinediones in patients with reduced LVEF.
Nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers like diltiazem and verapamil are not recommended for patients with HF or reduced LVEF.
